standard_prerequisites.name: The notion of a standard shrinking of a complete devissage
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, definition labelled definition-shrink-complete (statement, proof line 1363), together with the item labels item-shrink-base-complete, item-shrink-on-Y-complete and item-shrink-on-X-complete declared inside the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes what has to be produced in each of the three statements: a standard shrinking whose base lies in a given standard open neighbourhood, or whose last scheme is a given W times the base, or whose source lies in a given open U.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change of a complete devissage at a point
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-base-change-complete-at-x, invoked at proof line 1384
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies, in part (1), that the base changed data still form a complete devissage at the image point, so that restricting to a standard open neighbourhood of the base gives a standard shrinking.

standard_prerequisites.name: The one step shrinking lemmas
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-shrink, invoked at proof lines 1384 and 1389 with the item references item-shrink-on-Y and item-shrink-on-X, and again at proof line 1417
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides one step of shrinking at the level of the last scheme or at the level of the source, which the proof iterates along the devissage in parts (2) and (3); the item labels are navigation pointers outside the counted span and carry the label string itself as their number because they are item labels, not indexed tags.

core_obligations: Part (1): for a standard open neighbourhood S' of s, combine base change of the complete devissage at the image point with the one step shrinking lemma to see that the restricted data X', Z'_k and Y'_k form a standard shrinking (proof lines 1382-1385).

Part (2): for a standard open W of Y_n, apply the one step shrinking lemma at the level of the last scheme to the one step devissage of the cokernel of alpha_{n-1} over Y_{n-1} over S at the point y_{n-1}, obtaining a shrinking with Y'_n = W times S'; then repeat this procedure for the cokernel of alpha_{n-2} over Y_{n-2}, continuing down the devissage until the level of Y_1, and assemble the successive bases into the required standard shrinking (proof lines 1387-1402).

Part (3): by induction on the length of the complete devissage, first apply the one step shrinking lemma at the level of the source to the one step devissage of the module over X over S at the point x with X' inside U; if the length is one this is enough, and otherwise the induction hypothesis gives a shrinking of the tail of the devissage with Y''_1 inside Y'_1, after which one more one step shrinking at the level of the last scheme produces the final data (proof lines 1404-1425).
proof_roadmap: Part (1) by base change of the devissage and one shrinking step (proof lines 1382-1385).
Part (2) by iterating the one step shrinking at the level of the last scheme down the devissage (proof lines 1387-1402).
Part (3) by induction on the length of the devissage, one shrinking step at the source and one at the last scheme (proof lines 1404-1425).
difficulty_reason: The lemma records that a complete devissage can always be shrunk: any standard open neighbourhood of the base, of the last scheme in the devissage, or of the point in the source can be met by an appropriate standard shrinking (statement lines 1360-1380, tag 05HM). The first part is a base change argument, but the other two require real iteration: part (2) walks down the devissage applying the one step shrinking lemma at the level of the last scheme and re-assembles the successive bases, and part (3) proceeds by induction on the length of the devissage, first shrinking at the level of the source and then shrinking the tail of the devissage inside the scheme so obtained. The iteration and re-assembly are the substance, so the claim is H2.
